name: Compilers and Language Processing
description: How a program in a high-level language becomes machine code: lexical analysis, parsing, semantic analysis, intermediate representation, code generation and optimisation.

topics.name: The Structure of a Compiler
topics.summary: The phases of translation and why the front end is separated from the back end.

subtopics.name: Phases of Compilation
subtopics.summary: Front end, middle end and back end, and what each phase produces.

objectives.text: Name the phases of a compiler and the output of each
Explain the benefit of separating the front end from the back end
Distinguish a compiler from an interpreter

subtopics.name: Defining a Language
subtopics.summary: Syntax versus semantics, and grammars as specification.

objectives.text: Distinguish syntax from semantics with an example of each kind of error
Read a context-free grammar in BNF notation
Explain what a grammar does not specify about a language

subtopics.name: Symbol Tables and Scope
subtopics.summary: Recording declarations and resolving names across nested scopes.

objectives.text: Describe the structure of a symbol table supporting nested scopes
Resolve a name to its declaration under lexical scoping rules
Explain the difference between static and dynamic scoping

topics.name: Lexical Analysis
topics.summary: Turning a character stream into tokens — the first and simplest phase.

subtopics.name: Tokens and Regular Expressions
subtopics.summary: Lexemes, token classes and the regular expressions that describe them.

objectives.text: Write regular expressions describing identifiers, numbers and operators
Tokenise a short source fragment by hand
Explain the maximal munch rule for token recognition

subtopics.name: Finite Automata
subtopics.summary: DFAs and NFAs, and their equivalence to regular expressions.

objectives.text: Construct a DFA recognising a given regular language
Convert an NFA to an equivalent DFA by subset construction
Explain why finite automata suffice for lexical analysis

subtopics.name: Implementing a Lexer
subtopics.summary: Hand-written versus generated lexers, and lexical error handling.

objectives.text: Describe how a table-driven lexer operates
Handle a lexical error and recover to continue scanning
Explain how keywords are distinguished from identifiers

topics.name: Parsing
topics.summary: Recovering the structure the grammar implies from a flat token stream.

subtopics.name: Context-Free Grammars and Parse Trees
subtopics.summary: Derivations, parse trees, ambiguity and precedence.

objectives.text: Derive a string from a context-free grammar and draw its parse tree
Identify an ambiguous grammar and give two parse trees for one string
Rewrite a grammar to encode operator precedence and associativity

subtopics.name: Top-Down Parsing
subtopics.summary: Recursive descent, LL(1), FIRST and FOLLOW sets and left recursion.

objectives.text: Write a recursive descent parser for a small grammar
Compute FIRST and FOLLOW sets for a grammar
Eliminate left recursion so a grammar becomes suitable for top-down parsing

subtopics.name: Bottom-Up Parsing
subtopics.summary: Shift-reduce parsing, LR items and parser generators.

objectives.text: Trace a shift-reduce parse using a stack and input buffer
Explain why LR parsing handles a larger grammar class than LL
Identify a shift-reduce conflict and its cause

topics.name: Semantic Analysis
topics.summary: Checking what the grammar cannot express — that a syntactically valid program makes sense.

subtopics.name: Type Checking
subtopics.summary: Type rules, inference on expressions and type errors.

objectives.text: Apply typing rules to determine the type of an expression
Identify a type error that parsing cannot detect
Explain implicit coercion and its risks

subtopics.name: Attribute Grammars and Semantic Rules
subtopics.summary: Synthesised and inherited attributes, and syntax-directed translation.

objectives.text: Distinguish synthesised from inherited attributes
Annotate a parse tree using a set of semantic rules
Describe syntax-directed translation of an expression

subtopics.name: Error Detection and Reporting
subtopics.summary: Producing diagnostics a programmer can act on, and recovering to find more.

objectives.text: Classify an error as lexical, syntactic or semantic
Explain what makes a compiler error message useful
Describe a strategy for error recovery during parsing

topics.name: Intermediate Representation
topics.summary: A form that is easier to analyse and optimise than either source or machine code.

subtopics.name: Forms of Intermediate Code
subtopics.summary: Three-address code, abstract syntax trees and static single assignment.

objectives.text: Translate an expression into three-address code
Explain the advantage of an IR over direct source-to-target translation
Describe static single assignment form and its benefit for analysis

subtopics.name: Control Flow Graphs
subtopics.summary: Basic blocks, edges and the representation optimisation works on.

objectives.text: Partition a code sequence into basic blocks
Construct a control flow graph from three-address code
Identify a loop in a control flow graph

subtopics.name: Translating Language Constructs
subtopics.summary: Lowering conditionals, loops, arrays and procedure calls to IR.

objectives.text: Translate an if-else and a while loop into three-address code with labels
Generate address computation for an array access
Describe the IR produced for a procedure call and return

topics.name: Code Generation and Optimisation
topics.summary: Producing target code that is correct first and fast second.

subtopics.name: Instruction Selection and Register Allocation
subtopics.summary: Mapping IR to instructions and assigning limited registers.

objectives.text: Select target instructions for a three-address statement
Explain register allocation as a graph colouring problem
Describe what spilling is and why it costs performance

subtopics.name: Local Optimisation
subtopics.summary: Constant folding, common subexpression elimination and dead code removal.

objectives.text: Apply constant folding and propagation to a basic block
Eliminate a common subexpression and state the saving
Identify dead code that can be removed safely

subtopics.name: Loop and Global Optimisation
subtopics.summary: Loop-invariant code motion, strength reduction and unrolling.

objectives.text: Move a loop-invariant computation out of a loop
Apply strength reduction to a loop induction variable
Explain the trade-off loop unrolling makes between size and speed
